# ExportOptions

Namespace `Nfty.Core.Publish` in assembly `Nfty.Core`.

```csharp
public record ExportOptions
```

Exactly what leaves the machine.

## Remarks

**Four independent axes, not a mode switch** — the art, each of the two metadata sets, and the source book — because the reasons people share a collection do not line up into a ladder. A marketplace wants less than a buyer, who wants less than a collaborator, but a sealed review copy is not a point on that line at all.

**Every member is `init`-only with a default**, so a new axis is additive at every existing call site — the same rule the manifests follow for schema evolution.

**The passphrase is deliberately NOT here.** It is a parameter of the operation, not a property of the description: this record is the thing a front-end holds in a view model, binds to checkboxes, and would quite reasonably log or serialize while debugging. A secret that lives in it is a secret waiting to be written to disk by accident.

### ImageBaseUri { #p-imagebaseuri }

```csharp
public string? ImageBaseUri { get; init; }
```

Where the uploaded `images/` folder lives. Each `image` link becomes this followed by the image's FILE NAME: `ipfs://CID/` gives `ipfs://CID/1.png`.

**Remarks**

By file name, not by path inside the export: uploading the `images/` folder to IPFS (Pinata, NFT.Storage, `ipfs add -r`) gives a CID whose root IS that folder's contents, so the right link has no `images/` in it. It is also the only order that works: the metadata carries this address, so the art has to be uploaded (and addressed) first.

Export-only; the cooked Set keeps its relative paths. Must be absolute, use the scheme `ipfs`, `https`, `http` or `ar`, and end with `/` ([`MarketplaceRules.BaseUriProblem()`](Nfty.Core.Publish.MarketplaceRules.md#m-baseuriproblem-system-string-system-string)). Never guessed or repaired. Null leaves the relative path and the plan says so.

### IncludeCollectionMetadata { #p-includecollectionmetadata }

```csharp
public bool IncludeCollectionMetadata { get; init; }
```

Write `collection.json`, the contract-level metadata (OpenSea's `contractURI` shape).

**Remarks**

**An axis of its own.** It is not an item file and no Set contains it; the export makes it. On for [`ExportPreset.Marketplace`](Nfty.Core.Publish.ExportPreset.md#f-marketplace), off elsewhere. The name and symbol come from the Set, the description from its metadata.

### IncludeCookBook { #p-includecookbook }

```csharp
public bool IncludeCookBook { get; init; }
```

Ship the source `.cbk` alongside the Set.

**Remarks**

A flag, with the PATH supplied to the operation — for the same reason the passphrase is. A Set records only its book's hash, never the book, so the caller is the one that knows which file is meant; but a preset has to be able to say "include it" without knowing where it lives, or [`ExportPreset.FullProject`](Nfty.Core.Publish.ExportPreset.md#f-fullproject) could not be a preset at all.

### IncludeSetManifest { #p-includesetmanifest }

```csharp
public bool IncludeSetManifest { get; init; }
```

Include `set.json` — the Set's own record: seed, source-book hash, rarity table.

**Remarks**

**On by default, off for [`ExportPreset.Marketplace`](Nfty.Core.Publish.ExportPreset.md#f-marketplace)**: a public drop has no use for the seed and the book's hash, and a seed that should stay private until the reveal is otherwise published with the art. Without it nfty cannot reopen the export as a full Set; a suitable art/metadata export can still reopen as a read-only [`MarketplaceBundle`](Nfty.Core.Publish.MarketplaceBundle.md). A sealed export requires the manifest.

### Models { #p-models }

```csharp
public bool Models { get; init; }
```

Include `models/` — the 3D model written for each asset at cook time.

**Remarks**

**On by default, and on for [`ExportPreset.Marketplace`](Nfty.Core.Publish.ExportPreset.md#f-marketplace) too** — a marketplace shows a glb `animation_url` as a 3D viewer, so the models are part of the listing, not an extra. A Set cooked without models has no `models/`, so the flag then changes nothing and the plan never mentions the part.

**The models are copied as cooked and never re-rendered**, so the debug mark ([`ExportOptions.NumberWatermark`](Nfty.Core.Publish.ExportOptions.md#p-numberwatermark)), which stamps only the art on the way out, cannot reach one: a model's texture is the unstamped asset.

### NftyMetadata { #p-nftymetadata }

```csharp
public bool NftyMetadata { get; init; }
```

Include `nfty/` — per-asset DNA, the seed, and the color rolled on every layer.

**Remarks**

The axis with a consequence worth stating: this is the file that records HOW each asset came out the way it did. It is what a buyer wants and what a public listing has no use for.

### NumberWatermark { #p-numberwatermark }

```csharp
public bool NumberWatermark { get; init; }
```

Stamp each asset's set number into a corner of its art.

**Remarks**

**A debug mark, and it says so.** Loose sprites lose their filenames the moment they are dragged into an engine, a sprite editor or a chat window, and a folder of five hundred near-identical characters is unsortable without one. The number stamped is the asset's own set number, so a stamped sprite cross-references `nfty/NNNN.json` with nothing else having to be recorded.

**It is destructive, so it only ever happens on the way OUT.** The export renders a stamped copy and ships that; the author's Set is never touched. A stamped export is for working with, not for minting - which is why it is a box you tick rather than part of any preset.

### SpriteSheet { #p-spritesheet }

```csharp
public bool SpriteSheet { get; init; }
```

Also stitch every asset into one `spritesheet.png`.

**Remarks**

**A fifth content axis, not a fifth shape.** It travels with the export rather than replacing it — a sheet is what an engine loads and the numbered PNGs are what a marketplace mints, and a collection handed to a game developer usually wants both. So it is a checkbox beside the other four and not a preset, and it is the one entry in an export that does not exist on disk until the export makes it.

Cells across the sheet, or null to fall to the squarest grid that fits.

**Remarks**

**Null is a real answer and not a zero.** Most people want "just lay it out", and asking two numbers of somebody who has no opinion is how a checkbox becomes a form. The default is `SpriteSheet.Fit`, and either number may be given alone — the other follows from the count.

### MatchingPreset() { #m-matchingpreset }

```csharp
public ExportPreset? MatchingPreset();
```

Which preset these options ARE, or null when they are a combination of the author's own.

**Returns.** The preset these options equal, or null.

**Remarks**

Answered by comparing content rather than by remembering which button was pressed, so a screen cannot go on claiming a preset after a box beneath it was unticked. The note is ignored: it is a message to a person, not part of the export's shape. So are the marketplace VALUES (base URI, naming, links, royalty): they fill in what a content axis writes, they do not choose what leaves. [`ExportPreset.Marketplace`](Nfty.Core.Publish.ExportPreset.md#f-marketplace) STARTS at token-id naming, but a different naming does not un-name it.

**[`ExportOptions.Shape`](Nfty.Core.Publish.ExportOptions.md#p-shape) is ignored too, and that is the correction.** A preset names WHAT LEAVES the machine; folder-or-file is how it is packed, and the two are separate questions — which is why the shape controls sit in their own column rather than among the content boxes. Comparing it meant every preset came un-named the moment the shape was changed: ticking all four content boxes and choosing Single file left Full project lit until the shape was touched and then lit nothing at all, and Marketplace did the same in the other direction, unnoticed because its default shape is the common one. The presets still START at a shape apiece ([`ExportPreset.FullProject`](Nfty.Core.Publish.ExportPreset.md#f-fullproject) at a folder, the rest at an archive), which is what a starting point is for.

They stay distinguishable without it: the four differ in content or in the seal, never in shape alone.
